newsitem.title: USA: Investors urge CBES to improve value.
newsitem.headline: Investors urge CBES to improve value.

text.p: Connecticut investors Susan and Jerome Davis said Tuesday they asked CBES Bancorp Inc. to cut expenses and put what they called its excess capital to work in an effort to improve the value of the company's stock.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the couple, which holds 9.48 percent of the company, said Jerome Davis sent a Feb. 12 letter to each board member that urged CBES to use its "excess capital" to repurchase stock and declare a large regular dividend and a large special dividend.
In the letter, Davis said the Excelsior Springs, Mo., company maintains an excessive capital ratio of 18.9 percent.
At its current price/earnings ratio of 12.9 and with its stock trading at 92 percent of book value, the price of its stock has no cause to rise, Davis said.
"However a reduction in expenses should improve the price of the common stock to about $18.00 per share," he said.
Expenses as a percentage of its assets are 2.79 percent, its highest level of the past three quarters, he said.
The Greenwich couple said it bought 14,700 CBES shares between Jan. 13 and Feb. 10 at prices ranging from $14.375 to $15.50, raising its total stake to 97,200 shares.
